submissions.findingTextShort: A six-week randomized study in healthy women increased plasma flavonoid exposure with 500 mg/day rutin but did not materially improve key oxidative-damage markers.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In 18 healthy women, a randomized single-blind placebo-controlled six-week trial of rutin 500 mg/day increased plasma flavonoid exposure but did not materially improve key oxidative-damage markers versus placebo. Short-term blood chemistry and liver-function measures did not show an adverse signal. This is a useful PK/biomarker null and not evidence of broad vascular or metabolic clinical benefit.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very small healthy-volunteer study; biomarker exposure and short-term tolerability do not establish disease prevention or long-term safety.

submissions.findingTextShort: A three-month placebo-controlled trial in type 2 diabetes reported glycemic, lipid, inflammatory, and oxidative-marker changes with 500 mg/day rutin; these are disease-specific surrogate outcomes.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 50 patients with type 2 diabetes tested rutin 500 mg/day for three months and reported changes in glycemic, lipid, inflammatory, and oxidative-stress markers. These are disease-specific surrogate outcomes and should not be converted into proof of cardiovascular-event reduction, diabetes remission, or general metabolic benefit in healthy users.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small disease-specific trial with surrogate outcomes; defined rutin is not a generic standardized botanical extract.
